resources.string: Granny\'s Knees is a playful weather-sensitivity indicator, not medical advice, a diagnosis, or a forecast of how you\'ll feel. Weather is only weather.

Granny's Knees turns the hourly forecast into a 1–10 index from twelve-hour changes in temperature, humidity, and surface pressure. A higher number means more provocative weather in the model. It is not a measurement of your pain, and it does not say the weather caused a flare.

The evidence that weather and joint symptoms line up is mixed. Correlation is not causation. Your joints may disagree with the number.

If the index is high and someone wants help moving a sofa, you have something to point at.
A little science. A little superstition.
This is a playful weather index, not a diagnosis and not a prediction of how you will feel. You can use it without recording symptoms. Anything you do record stays on this phone.
How data stays on this phone is described in the privacy policy.

Each point on the Today curve scores how the weather is changing around that hour — not how hot or humid it is in absolute terms. Temperature, humidity, and a feels-like gap use a short four-hour slope. Pressure still uses the change over twelve hours.

Cooling counts more than warming. Rising humidity and a growing feels-like gap (air holding while it feels colder) push the index up. Rising pressure tends to pull it down. Steady weather sits near the middle of the 1–10 scale (about 5.5).

The feed is outdoor only, so indoor heating cycles are invisible. Weather is the shared baseline. Personal is the real-feel series. The Settings sliders are not “high versus low” or “hot versus cold” — they ask how much each factor influences you. Higher influence means that factor weighs more in Personal. When “Use Feel reports to tune real-feel” is on, Feel check-ins can gently adjust those influence levels after ten consecutive usable reports: saves within fifteen minutes count as one moment; each consecutive counted moment must be at least forty-five minutes apart. Opting out keeps recording but does not change influence. If you leave every slider at no adjustment and opt out of Feel tuning, there is no Personal curve.

For best results, report every hour on the hour — especially when it feels especially bad or especially good. Those extremes help hone the values. You cannot currently go back in time to file a Feel report for earlier in the day; each save is for now.

Blank spots on the curve mean missing data or an incomplete slope or pressure window — never a filled-in zero. The big number and band use Weather; the five-day columns show Standard on the left and Personal on the right when Personal is active. Feel ratings stay separate from the weather number. This is a weather-change index, not medical advice.
Use Feel reports to tune real-feel
When on, spaced Feel check-ins can gently adjust Personal after ten consecutive usable reports. When off, Feel is record-only.
Removes stored Feel check-ins used for real-feel tuning. Journal symptom reports stay.
Let Granny speak her mind freely
When on, Granny may use the occasional salty word and a few more theatrical complaints. Off keeps the commentary family-friendly.

These sliders are about influence — how much each weather factor affects your real-feel — not whether pressure is high or low, or whether it is hot or cold.

0 — that factor does not change Personal; stay with the standard index for it.
10 — that factor strongly influences how you feel, more than the others.
Choose light or dark, or match the phone.
Clears saved history and today\'s draft figure on this phone.
